stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = a(x - p)(x - q)\), where \(a\), \(p\), and \(q\) are constants with \(a > 0\) and \(p < 0 < q\). Which of the following must be true?

choices.D: Whether \(f(0)\) is positive or negative depends on the value of \(a\)

solution: \(f(0) = a(0 - p)(0 - q) = a \cdot p \cdot q\).
Since \(p < 0\) and \(q > 0\), the product \(pq\) is negative, and multiplying by \(a > 0\) keeps it negative. So \(f(0) < 0\).
Graphically: the parabola opens upward and its \(x\)-intercepts lie on opposite sides of the \(y\)-axis, so the graph is below the \(x\)-axis at \(x = 0\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(f(0) = a(-p)(-q) = apq\). Because \(p < 0 < q\), the product \(pq\) is negative, so \(f(0) < 0\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(f(0) = 0\) only if \(0\) is a zero of \(f\), that is, if \(p = 0\) or \(q = 0\). Neither is 0 here.
explanation.C: Correct. \(f(0) = apq\), and \(pq < 0\) because \(p\) and \(q\) have opposite signs; with \(a > 0\), \(f(0)\) is negative.
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(a > 0\) is given, so the sign of \(f(0) = apq\) is determined by \(pq\), which is negative.

verify:
a, q = symbols('a q', positive=True)
p = symbols('p', negative=True)
x = symbols('x')
f0 = (a*(x - p)*(x - q)).subs(x, 0)
assert f0.is_negative
assert (2*(x + 1)*(x - 3)).subs(x, 0) == -6
assert choices[answer] == r'\(f(0) < 0\)'
assert len(set(choices.values())) == 4
